pages.title: Hello and Goodbye
pages.can: Say hello and goodbye to anyone.
pages.grammarNote: One word, two jobs. שָׁלוֹם means peace, and Israelis use it both to greet and to leave. לְהִתְרָאוֹת is only for leaving: see you later. הֵי is casual, for friends.

pages.title: Good Morning to Good Night
pages.can: Greet people at any time of day.
pages.grammarNote: The adjective comes after the noun and matches it. In Hebrew the describing word follows the noun: בֹּקֶר טוֹב is morning good. It also matches the noun: צָהֳרַיִם is a plural form, so it takes טוֹבִים, not טוֹב.

pages.title: How Are You?
pages.can: Ask how someone is, to a man or to a woman.
pages.grammarNote: Your: an ending that changes for a man or a woman. מַה שְׁלוֹמְךָ? asks a man; מַה שְׁלוֹמֵךְ? asks a woman. The ending ךָ means your (to a man) and ךְ means your (to a woman). מָה נִשְׁמָע? works for anyone, so it is the safe choice when you are not sure.

With a masculine noun the other set is used: שְׁלוֹשָׁה. Start with the counting set; you will meet the other with nouns in the shop unit.

pages.title: Say It About Yourself

pages.grammarNote: Describing yourself: man's and woman's forms again. A man says אֲנִי תַּיָּר, a woman אֲנִי תַּיֶּרֶת. The question changes with the person asked: מָה אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה? to a man, מָה אַתְּ עוֹשָׂה? to a woman.

grammar.point: Describing yourself: man's and woman's forms again
grammar.body: A man says אֲנִי תַּיָּר, a woman אֲנִי תַּיֶּרֶת. The question changes with the person asked: מָה אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה? to a man, מָה אַתְּ עוֹשָׂה? to a woman.

pages.title: First Words Check
pages.can: Show you can greet, be polite, count and introduce yourself.
pages.grammarNote: Putting the first level together. This check mixes every unit of the first level. One new phrase: מָה הַמַּצָּב? is another casual how's it going, built like מָה נִשְׁמָע?.
